latest_release.name: Release 2.45.3 LTS
latest_release.body:
## Known issues

- On Async Edge environments, an invalid update schedule date can be displayed when browsing a snapshot

### Known issues with Podman support

- Podman environments aren't supported by auto-onboarding script
- It's not possible to add Podman environments via socket, when running a Portainer server on Docker (and vice versa)
- Support for only CentOS 9, Podman 5 rootful

## Changes

### Breaking changes

- Portainer no longer trusts TLS certificates issued by eMudhra (emSign), following the compromise of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs (CVE-2026-111943). Connections to services that present an affected certificate, including OAuth/OIDC and LDAPS providers, registries and Git hosts, will fail after the upgrade. If your single sign-on or LDAP provider is affected, only the initial admin will be able to sign in. Check your services before upgrading. [See this FAQ for details.](https://hubs.li/Q04B-qY30)

### Security improvements

- Rejected Compose and Swarm stacks using `volumes_from` when non-administrators create, update, start or redeploy them with `Hide bind mounts for non-administrators` enabled, which let them inherit another container's host bind mounts
- Updated the Go toolchain to 1.26.10, fixing CVE-2026-56857 and CVE-2026-78663 (both Critical), along with CVE-2026-111943, CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-97031, CVE-2026-94440, CVE-2026-94439, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78667, CVE-2026-78660, CVE-2026-78659, CVE-2026-56866, CVE-2026-94448 and CVE-2026-97030
- Removed the eMudhra emSign root certificates from the CA bundle in Linux images, and rejected certificate chains that contain the compromised eMudhra intermediates (CVE-2026-111943). [See this FAQ for details.](https://hubs.li/Q04B-qY30)
- Updated [golang.org/x/net](http://golang.org/x/net) to 0.60.0, fixing CVE-2026-78663 (Critical), CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78660 and CVE-2026-78659 (all High)
- Updated helm in the kubectl shell image to v4.3.1, taking its Go toolchain to 1.27.2 and oras.land/oras-go/v2 to 2.6.2, fixing CVE-2026-39821 (Critical) and CVE-2026-50163 (High)
- Restricted kubeconfig tokens to the /api/endpoints/{id}/kubernetes proxy, so they are rejected with a 403 on every other API route, including admin-only routes and the Docker proxy. Kubeconfigs downloaded after upgrading carry a separate token per environment, limited to that environment 

### Bug fixes

- Fixed starting a container with an empty request body failing with a 400 error on Docker standalone and Swarm agent environments 
- Fixed GitOps sources starting a new poll while the previous one was still running, which could pile up overlapping redeploys on slow repositories. A poll that is still running now causes the next scheduled poll to be skipped
- Fixed GitOps workflows showing the Git reference and file path status as unknown after a stack was manually redeployed from Git. A manual redeploy now records these statuses for the stack's workflow artifact
- Fixed the YAML tab on the Kubernetes node details page going blank after switching tabs or refocusing the browser, and restored the missing gap between the tab content and the Applications table
- Fixed DockerHub pull rate limits and agent version detection failing on Docker engines newer than API 1.47, and, in BE, non-admin users with environment access getting 403 errors on `/agent/docker` and `/agent/host` routes, which left Swarm node selectors empty
- Fixed the search box on the Authentication logs page not filtering events by username

## Deprecated and removed features

None.

detail.readme: **Portainer Community Edition** is a free, lightweight container management UI for Docker, Swarm, Podman, Kubernetes, and ACI environments. It is provided as-is, at no cost, for the convenience of homelab operators, hobbyists, students, and anyone experimenting with containers on their own hardware. **Portainer Business Edition** builds on the same open-source base and adds the features, hardening, and commercial support that production and enterprise environments require (RBAC, GitOps, edge management, audit, SSO, and more). - [Find out more about Portainer Business Edition features](https://www.portainer.io/features) - [Take3 – get 3 free nodes of Portainer Business for as long as you want them](https://www.portainer.io/take-3) - [Get started with Portainer BE](https://www.portainer.io/get-started) ## Intended use Portainer CE is designed for homelabs, learning environments, personal projects, and other non-production deployments. It is not intended for, or supported in, business, production, or any other environment where uptime, security posture, or data integrity matter. It is provided without support, without warranty (express or implied), and without any commitment as to fitness for a particular purpose. There is no SLA, no guaranteed response to issues, and no roadmap commitment. If you run Portainer CE, you are choosing to self-support, and you should be comfortable reading source, filing your own issues, and troubleshooting on your own. If you need Portainer in a production or business-critical context, or you want commercial support, use Portainer Business Edition. ## Latest version Portainer CE is updated periodically, with no guarantees on cadence, and is provided as-is and without support. Business Edition releases will be more frequent than Community Edition. [![latest version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/portainer/portainer?color=%2344cc11&label=Latest%20release&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/portainer/portainer/releases/latest) ## Getting started - [Deploy Portainer](https://docs.portainer.io/start/install-ce) - [Documentation](https://docs.portainer.io) - [Contribute to the project](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Getting help Portainer CE has no official support channel. You may find help from other users via GitHub Issues and the community Slack, but any assistance you receive there is voluntary, best-effort, and provided by other community members rather than by Portainer. It is not a substitute for commercial support. - Issues: https://github.com/portainer/portainer/issues - Community: [https://www.portainer.io/join-our-community](https://www.portainer.io/join-our-community) If you need commercial support, guaranteed response, or you are running Portainer in a production or business-critical context, buy a supported version at [portainer.io](https://www.portainer.io/). ## Reporting bugs and contributing - Want to report a bug or request a feature? Open [an issue](https://github.com/portainer/portainer/issues/new/choose). Please note that filing an issue does not create any obligation on the project to respond, triage, or fix it. - Want to help build **_Portainer_**? Follow our [contribution guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) to build it locally and open a pull request. ## Security For information about reporting security vulnerabilities, please see our [Security Policy](SECURITY.md). ## Work for us If you are a developer, and our code in this repo makes sense to you, we would love to hear from you. We are always on the hunt for good devs, either freelance or employed. Drop us a line at contribute@portainer.io with your details, or visit our [careers page](https://apply.workable.com/portainer/). ## Licensing Portainer is licensed under the zlib license. See [LICENSE](./LICENSE) for reference. Portainer also contains code from open source projects. See [ATTRIBUTIONS.md](./ATTRIBUTIONS.md) for a list.
